findings.scope: Agent Server on the supported local-filesystem coordination model
findings.evidence: ConversationLease stores owner_instance_id plus monotonically increasing generation; takeover increments generation; renew/guarded_write require owner+generation; EventService installs the lease-backed write guard into persistent conversation state/event writes.
findings.boundary: Do not generalize to NFS/network filesystems. EventLog explicitly warns LocalFileStore flock coordination is unreliable there.

findings.evidence: LocalFileStore writes are per-file atomic replacements. ConversationState.append_event persists the event first, then assigns leaf_event_id, whose public-field autosave persists base_state.json separately.
findings.boundary: Event file plus base_state HEAD are not one atomic transaction.

findings.evidence: At the exact v1.44.1 target, append_event calls EventLog.append before leaf_event_id autosave. Resume deserializes persisted base_state, creates EventLog, and rebuilds the active view from path_to_root(_resolve_active_leaf()). _resolve_active_leaf returns a persisted non-null leaf_event_id directly. Therefore a crash/failure after event-file commit but before HEAD autosave can leave that just-written event outside the resumed active branch when the old leaf was non-null.
findings.caution: This is a code-level recoverability gap, not a claim of observed user data corruption. The source comment saying HEAD is recoverable from the just-appended event is not, by itself, evidence that this non-null stale-HEAD case is reconciled.

findings.evidence: Modern MCP discovery exposes supported versions/capabilities plus TTL/cache scope; client behavior is protocol-version sensitive.
findings.safe_rule: Cache capability knowledge only under negotiated protocol + server identity when available + unexpired TTL + matching cache/authorization scope. Otherwise REVALIDATE.

findings.evidence: readOnly/destructive/idempotent/openWorld annotations are descriptive hints and are untrusted unless the server is trusted.
findings.safe_rule: Never bypass confirmation, authorization, sandboxing, or effect verification solely from tool annotations.

findings.evidence: When the tasks extension is negotiated and the server durably creates the task before returning its handle, persisting taskId allows reconnect plus tasks/get recovery.
findings.boundary: A cancellation acknowledgement is cooperative intent, not proof the task stopped. Treat terminal task status/result as stronger completion evidence.

findings.evidence: Checkpoint/replay durability does not itself make external side effects exactly once; provider/application idempotency keys, CAS/preconditions, or exact effect readback remain required.
findings.external_issue_scope: Issues #8234 and #8702 were used only as user-reported counterexample/risk evidence, not as maintainer-confirmed current defects.

counterexamples: A generation lease proved on local filesystem does not prove safe distributed coordination on NFS/network storage.
Atomic replacement of each file does not imply atomicity across event file + base_state snapshot.
A persisted non-null stale HEAD can exclude a later event file from the active branch after resume; legacy fallback only applies when leaf_event_id is null.
MCP capability discovery older than ttlMs or from the wrong cacheScope is stale evidence, not permanent capability authority.
A tool annotation that says readOnly/destructive/idempotent is not an enforcement mechanism.
A durable task handle proves resumability only within the server's retention/terminal-result semantics; cancel ACK is not stop proof.
Workflow/checkpoint replay without idempotency/CAS can repeat an external effect after ambiguous completion.
